subsystems.name: Prospecting and excavation
subsystems.role: find and dig up ice-bearing regolith or collect atmosphere.

subsystems.name: Water processing
subsystems.role: turn icy dirt into clean water and then into hydrogen and oxygen.

subsystems.name: Atmosphere processing (Mars)
subsystems.role: use the CO2 atmosphere as a feedstock.

subsystems.name: Regolith processing
subsystems.role: release oxygen locked in metal oxides in the soil.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic storage and distribution
subsystems.role: keep liquid oxygen and methane cold and move them where needed.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: run reactors that are energy-hungry and dump waste heat in vacuum.
parts: fission surface power unit or solar arrays

buildSteps.title: Prospect the site
buildSteps.detail: Orbiters map hydrogen and ice deposits; landers and rovers then drill or scoop to confirm how much water is really there and how deep.

buildSteps.title: Excavate feedstock
buildSteps.detail: A digger or drill lifts ice-rich regolith into a hopper; on Mars a compressor can simply pull in CO2 from the air.

buildSteps.title: Release the water
buildSteps.detail: The regolith is sealed in a vessel and heated, so the ice sublimates and the vapour is captured and condensed.

buildSteps.title: Purify and split the water
buildSteps.detail: Electrolysis separates water into oxygen and hydrogen; the oxygen is the main product for breathing and rocket oxidiser.

buildSteps.title: Make methane on Mars
buildSteps.detail: Hydrogen is reacted with CO2 in the Sabatier process to give methane and water, and the water is electrolysed again, closing most of the loop.

buildSteps.title: Extract oxygen from soil
buildSteps.detail: Where water is scarce, regolith is melted and a current drives oxygen out of the metal oxides, leaving alloy by-products.

buildSteps.title: Liquefy and store
buildSteps.detail: Product gases are cooled to liquids and kept in insulated tanks, which is difficult because they boil off over time.

buildSteps.title: Connect to the base
buildSteps.detail: Piped oxygen feeds the habitat life-support system, while methane and oxygen feed the ascent vehicle that brings crews home.

prerequisites.why: ISRU plants run continuously and need far more power than a rover; fission surface power has been tested on the ground but not flown.

prerequisites.tech: Cryogenic fluid management in low gravity
prerequisites.why: liquids boil off without careful insulation and refrigeration, and long-term storage has not been proven in space.
digging in abrasive dust and hard frozen ground has only been done at small scale.
lunar dust is sharp and abrasive and quickly damages moving parts and connectors.
a plant must run for years with minimal maintenance from astronauts.

pathway.milestone: MOXIE on NASA's Perseverance rover made oxygen from Martian CO2 between 2021 and 2023
pathway.unlocks: proof that a key ISRU reaction works on another planet.

pathway.milestone: small pilot plants on the Moon and Mars that produce oxygen and water for a few crews
pathway.unlocks: data on dust, wear and autonomy over long periods.

pathway.milestone: demonstration plants that fill a rocket's tanks from local materials
pathway.unlocks: much cheaper Mars missions, because most return propellant no longer has to be launched from Earth.

pathway.milestone: integrated refuelling and life-support farms at a permanent base
pathway.unlocks: bases that grow rather than depend on resupply from Earth.
